name: Telecommunications
business_model: Network operators: towers and network equipment, high-volume billing, multi-element customer contracts, decommissioning obligations for installed infrastructure.
regulatory_requirements: PTA licensing (Telecom Re-organization Act 1996); PTA type-approval and tariff oversight; SECP/PSX for listed operators; PEMRA where broadcast content is carried.

name: Manufacturing
business_model: Production entities: work in progress, standard costing, overhead absorption, warranty provisions, capital-intensive plant.
regulatory_requirements: SECP and PSX Listing Regulations for listed manufacturers; provincial environmental protection agencies; labour and factory legislation; FBR/provincial sales-tax regimes.

name: Retail
business_model: High-volume cash and card sales, shrinkage, supplier rebates, gift cards/loyalty programmes, leased store portfolios.
regulatory_requirements: Provincial sales-tax on services/retail where applicable; FBR for corporate tax; provincial consumer-protection authorities; SECP for listed retailers.

name: Banking and financial services
business_model: Regulated lenders: loan impairment (expected credit losses), interest recognition, regulatory capital and disclosures.
regulatory_requirements: SBP Prudential Regulations and Banking Companies Ordinance 1962; SBP inspection and reporting; SECP/PSX for listed banks; deposit protection (Deposit Protection Corporation).

name: Insurance
business_model: Risk pooling: premiums collected upfront, claims paid later. Life and general (non-life) businesses differ sharply — life carries long-duration policyholder liabilities, general carries short-tail claim cycles.
revenue_streams: Gross written premiums; reinsurance commissions; investment income on the float.
major_costs: Claims incurred; reinsurance premiums ceded; acquisition costs (commissions).
key_assets_liabilities: Technical reserves dominate the balance sheet: unearned premium reserves, outstanding claims (including IBNR — incurred but not reported), and life policyholder liabilities set by actuaries.
common_accounting_issues: Premium recognition cut-off (risk-attached vs cash-received); IBNR and outstanding-claim estimation; liability adequacy testing; reinsurance recoverable recognition; deferred acquisition costs.
significant_inherent_risks: Claim reserves are the largest estimate and highly judgemental — small assumption changes move profit materially. Premium cut-off errors and unrecorded IBNR understate liabilities.
typical_controls: Actuarial review of reserves; claims authorisation hierarchies; bordereau reconciliations with reinsurers; premium bordereau-to-ledger matching.
regulatory_requirements: SECP Insurance Division (Insurance Ordinance 2000, Insurance Rules 2017); solvency margin and statutory deposit requirements; Pakistan Insurance Corporation's former role now with private reinsurers.
notes: Auditors typically rely on actuarial specialists for reserve opinions (ISA 620). Reinsurance contracts must be read — not all 'reinsurance' transfers risk.
source_ref: CA Audit Intelligence Database — industry knowledge base

name: Construction and real estate development
business_model: Project-based: long-term contracts with milestone billings, variations, retention money and performance guarantees. Developers add off-plan sales and inventory of completed units.
revenue_streams: Contract revenue recognised over time as performance obligations are satisfied; sale of completed units.
major_costs: Subcontractor costs; materials; site overheads; financing costs during construction.
key_assets_liabilities: Contract assets/liabilities (unbilled revenue vs billings in excess); retention receivables; work in progress; completed-unit inventory.
common_accounting_issues: Measuring progress toward completion; forecasting total contract costs; recognising variations and claims; onerous contract provisions; capitalisation of borrowing costs.
significant_inherent_risks: Over-optimistic cost-to-complete forecasts flatter current margins — the classic construction failure pattern. Unapproved variations booked as revenue; onerous contracts not provided for.
typical_controls: Independent quantity-surveyor certifications; variation approval workflows; monthly cost-to-complete reforecasts reviewed by management.
regulatory_requirements: SECP for listed developers; provincial development authorities for project approvals; performance guarantees often bank-backed (ties to banking covenants).
notes: The Carillion case (CS-CAR-01) is the textbook warning: recognised profits on contracts that later proved loss-making.
source_ref: CA Audit Intelligence Database — industry knowledge base

name: Pharmaceuticals
business_model: Regulated manufacturing with patent-protected and generic portfolios. Revenue is net of complex deductions: chargebacks, rebates, returns and government price controls.
revenue_streams: Product sales (net of deductions); licensing and milestone income; toll manufacturing.
major_costs: R&D (mostly expensed); API and formulation costs; regulatory compliance; distribution.
key_assets_liabilities: Rebate and chargeback accruals; returns provisions; inventory subject to expiry; capitalised development costs where criteria are met.
common_accounting_issues: Estimating gross-to-net deductions; capitalisation vs expense of development costs; inventory NRV where products near expiry; licensing milestone recognition.
significant_inherent_risks: Gross-to-net estimates are large, judgemental and move with channel mix — under-accrued rebates overstate revenue. Expired inventory not written down.
typical_controls: Contract master-file controls for rebate terms; third-party administrator reconciliations for chargebacks; batch-level inventory tracking.
regulatory_requirements: DRAP (Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan) for pricing and registration; provincial drug authorities; export markets' regulators (FDA/EMA) for exporters.
notes: Chargeback/rebate accruals deserve the same scepticism as any large period-end estimate — subsequent settlement data is the key test.
source_ref: CA Audit Intelligence Database — industry knowledge base

name: Energy and utilities
business_model: Regulated or contracted generation and distribution: power purchase agreements (PPAs) with capacity and energy payments, tariff determinations by the regulator, and heavy upfront capital investment.
revenue_streams: Capacity payments; energy (variable) payments; late-payment surcharges; distribution margins.
major_costs: Fuel; debt servicing on project finance; operations and maintenance; decommissioning provisions.
key_assets_liabilities: Power plants (componentised for major overhauls); circular-debt receivables from government/offtakers; decommissioning and site-restoration provisions.
common_accounting_issues: Tariff true-ups and disputed receivables; impairment of plants where tariffs don't cover costs; decommissioning provision measurement; capitalisation of major overhauls vs expense.
significant_inherent_risks: Receivables from state offtakers may be subject to political/collection risk not reflected in provisions. Decommissioning estimates span decades.
typical_controls: PPA billing reconciliations to dispatch data; tariff-determination tracking; independent engineer assessments for major capex.
regulatory_requirements: NEPRA tariff determinations; CPPA-G settlements; provincial environmental approvals; SECP for listed IPPs.
notes: Circular debt is the sector's defining Pakistani feature — auditors must assess recoverability of government receivables with professional scepticism, not assumption.
source_ref: CA Audit Intelligence Database — industry knowledge base
